:::{#sol-extend-basis-practice}

One answer is $\vecf{e}_2$ and $\vecf{e}_3$.
The list $\vecf{v}_1$ is [linearly independent](#def-linearly-independent),
since $\vecf{v}_1 \ne \vzero$.
$\vecf{e}_2 = \tp{(0, 1, 0)}$ is not a multiple of $\vecf{v}_1$,
whose first two entries match,
so by @thm-add-outside-span the list $\vecf{v}_1, \vecf{e}_2$ is linearly independent.
Every vector in its [span](#def-span) has third entry $0$,
so $\vecf{e}_3$ is outside it,
and $\vecf{v}_1, \vecf{e}_2, \vecf{e}_3$ is linearly independent too.
These three vectors span $\reals^3$,
because $\tp{(x, y, z)} = x \vecf{v}_1 + (y - x) \vecf{e}_2 + z \vecf{e}_3$,
so they form a [basis](#def-basis) of $\reals^3$.
The pair $\vecf{e}_1$ and $\vecf{e}_3$ works too.

:::
